thread:
Ana (Support): HarborPay reported an abrupt throughput drop and a spike in 503s during their morning traffic burst at ~10:15 UTC. They see timeouts and ~11% 5xx.
Priyank (Sales): HarborPay is on a staged enterprise rollout with an availability clause. They're upset; cc @Tara (PM). Can we triage?
Tara (PM): Thanks Ana. Can you paste route, model, region, and a minimal repro? Also confirm if they saw this right after a deploy.
Ana (Support): Route: /v1/generate (harborpay-prod). Model: gpt-neo-quant-large. Seq ~550, concurrency ~160 from their side. Repro snippet: `POST /v1/generate {"model":"gpt-neo-quant-large","input":"~450 tokens"} -> 503 {"error":"instance overload"}`. They noted regression immediately after the 10:05 deploy window.
deploybot: Release v2026.08.20.10.05 -> eu-west-1 pool-9
Ben (Eng): Looking at telemetry: pod restarts and GPU OOMs in pool-9 starting ~10:07. The release included a kernel scheduling tweak for large KV cache workloads. Hypothesis: mem-residency spike under high concurrent small batches causing OOM and autoscaler churn.
Leo (Oncall): Confirmed OOMKills and ingress queuing. Nginx p95 jumped and autoscaler created/removed nodes rapidly.
Tara (PM): Quick mitigation options: (1) Per-route override to an fp16 variant (fast, small output drift). (2) Hot-route to dedicated EU pool (good perf, provisioning ~35-50m). (3) Rollback the scheduling tweak globally (~1h, higher blast radius). Need to weigh customer risk vs global impact.
Priyank (Sales): HarborPay asked for the least disruptive fix that preserves behavior. They prefer a temporary variant fallback + canary if that is low risk. They also want an ETA for RCA.
Ben (Eng): Practical plan: (A) Apply a 50-request canary routing to `gpt-neo-large-fp16` with 10% traffic, monitor p95/errors for 10m. (B) If stable, promote to 100% and keep under observation for 2h. If still bad, spin up dedicated EU pool. I'll push the override if Tara signs off.
Tara (PM): Go ahead with the canary. Action owners: Ben -> route override and logs, Leo -> infra monitoring and alerts, Ana -> coordinate with customer, Priyank -> comms.
Ben (Eng): Applying override: `PATCH /v1/routes/harborpay-prod` payload: `{"model_override": "gpt-neo-large-fp16", "canary_requests": 50, "canary_pct": 10 }`.
Leo (Oncall): Added temporary alert: `harborpay_error_rate > 2% for 1m` -> page eng-oncall. Watching node OOMs, pod restart rate, and ingress latency.
Ana (Support): Canary run: HarborPay reports first 50 requests p95 290ms, errors 0.6% (was 11%). They approved promoting to 100% and requested hourly status updates for 4 hours.
Priyank (Sales): I told them we've started the fallback and will monitor. They're relieved but want a firm RCA and timeline for a permanent fix.
Tara (PM): Backlog and acceptance criteria:
- P0 RCA ticket: reproduce mem surge with the scheduling tweak under high concurrency and propose fix. Owner: Ben. Due: 72h. Acceptance: repro + patch + perf regression test.
- P1: Product spec for per-route auto-fallback under memory pressure. Owner: Tara. Due: 2 sprints. Acceptance: spec + prototype and rollout plan.
- P1: Update deploy rollback runbook and escalation matrix. Owner: Leo. Due: 5 days. Acceptance: clear steps and communication templates.
- P2: Customer SLA impact calc and comms. Owner: Priyank. Due: 12h.
Ben (Eng): Created ticket HR-7700 and uploaded heapdumps and pod logs. Keeping override for 2h then reassess.
deploybot: HR-7700 created by ben (Eng)
Tara (PM): Customer closure criteria:
- HarborPay p95 < 400ms and error rate < 1% for 2 continuous hours
- RCA delivered with a remediation plan and scheduled fix canary in staging
- Per-route mitigation spec prioritized on the roadmap
Ana (Support): I'll check in with HarborPay in 1h and update the thread.
Leo (Oncall): If error rate rises >2% we escalate to runtime and consider capacity move.
Priyank (Sales): Sending an initial status note to HarborPay now. I'll include expected timelines and SLA note.
Ben (Eng): Promoted canary to 100% now. Monitoring.
Ana (Support): HarborPay confirms 100% routed; current p95 ~350ms and errors 0.4%. They asked for hourly updates for 4 hours and a postmortem.
Tara (PM): Thanks team. We'll track HR-7700 and create the product epic for auto-fallback. If fallback fails, we'll escalate to dedicated routing or rollback. :white_check_mark:
